title: Where your work is kept in {name}: this browser, this device, encrypted
description: {name} keeps your tasks and files in your browsers, encrypted, with no copy its servers can read. What can clear them, and how to keep a copy.
answer: In this browser, on this device, encrypted: your tasks, files, memory, settings and keys. No {name} server keeps them in a form it can read, except a site you publish. They are copied elsewhere only if you choose: a backup or a synced folder keeps your tasks and files; another of your devices that you add gets them too, with most of your settings and keys, sealed so only your devices can open them.
parts: In this browser, on this device

Each browser keeps its own {name}: what you do in Chrome isn’t in Safari, and what you do on your computer isn’t on your phone, until you add one to the other. So does each browser profile, the desktop app, and a copy of {name} that your organisation serves at its own address. Once you add your phone or another computer, your tasks, files and projects follow there within a minute while {name} is open on both, with most of your brains and settings, sealed so only your devices can open them; a project you keep on one device stays there.

Every file is sealed with a key made on this device, which never leaves it; what your devices keep in common is sealed with keys only they hold. With a lock, {name} opens only with your password or passkey.

A private window keeps nothing once it is closed. Clearing this site’s data, or your browser’s history with its cookies and site data, deletes everything here. A browser short of room may clear it too, and Safari may clear a site you haven’t opened for a week, unless it is on the Dock or the home screen.

A backup is one file with all your tasks and files: see {backup}. In Chrome and Edge, on a computer, {sync} keeps a copy in a folder that OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive or Google Drive syncs, once {name} offers it.
good: {settings} › {data} says how it stands in one line: when the last backup was made, for instance, or {unkept}
{space}, on the same page, shows how much room each part takes, and what can go to make room.
Installing {name} as an app, in Chrome or Edge or on a phone’s home screen, helps the browser keep its data.
A folder of your computer that you open in {name} stays where it is: in Chrome and Edge, {name} changes its files there; in other browsers, it works on a copy.

Your keys are never in a backup, a synced folder or a share. Another of your devices that you add gets most of them, sealed so only it can open them; there, the services that asked you to sign in ask again.
Where what you share goes, brain by brain, and every address {name} contacts: {files}.
fixes: Most often they are in another browser, profile or address. See {gone}.
This window is private. Open {name} in an ordinary window to keep your work.
ask: Where is my work kept, and when did I last back it up?
